label: late-prefix to early-copy window, boosted by an earlier n
explanation: Fires in a time window: from about step 2-3 of the original tokens through the <DEL> step and the first copy step (recall_idx <= 1). It peaks at t=4-6 and at <DEL>, where 25% of steps are active. It is never active at t=0-1 and rarely active after copy step 2. Magnitude depends strongly on whether n has already been input: sequences that start with n get the largest activations (first_tok=n has a 5.5x lift; all top examples begin with n, ramping up to about 1.0 of max over the prefix and <DEL>). An n at position 1 or 2 also drives it, more weakly. Without an earlier n it still fires weakly (mostly under 0.3 of max) in the same window, and somewhat more after u/w/f/digit starts. The predicate (n seen earlier, inside the window) gets dev F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.66. The bare window alone covers 89% of activations but with precision 0.17. Does not fire at the first two steps, in later copy steps, or in a way tied to the current input token.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & out_tok=n (+5.54), orig0=n (+5.26), next_out=n (+4.55), orig1=n (+4.27), orig2=n (+3.49), orig3=n (+2.77). Lower it: prev2_tok=- (-6.99), phase=2 (-6.19), phase=2 & in_tok=3 (-4.82), phase=2 & in_tok=b (-3.98).
